+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+DATA = Path("data/crashes.parquet")
+
+query = f"""
+SELECT
+    year(crash_date) AS year,
+    count(*) AS total_crash_reports,
+    sum(coalesce(number_of_pedestrians_injured, 0)) AS pedestrians_injured,
+    sum(coalesce(number_of_pedestrians_killed, 0)) AS pedestrians_killed,
+    sum(CASE WHEN coalesce(number_of_pedestrians_injured, 0)
+                  + coalesce(number_of_pedestrians_killed, 0) > 0
+             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty
+FROM read_parquet('{DATA.as_posix()}')
+WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+  AND crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+  AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+GROUP BY 1
+ORDER BY 1
+"""
+df = duckdb.connect().execute(query).df()
+df["pedestrian_casualties_per_1000_crash_reports"] = (
+    df["crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty"] / df["total_crash_reports"] * 1000
+)
+
+colors = {"blue": "#176B87", "red": "#C4473A", "gold": "#D49326", "ink": "#17232D", "muted": "#52616B", "grid": "#DCE3E7"}
+plt.rcParams.update({
+    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
+    "font.size": 11,
+    "axes.titlesize": 18,
+    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
+    "axes.labelsize": 11,
+    "axes.edgecolor": colors["grid"],
+    "axes.labelcolor": colors["muted"],
+    "xtick.color": colors["muted"],
+    "ytick.color": colors["muted"],
+    "figure.facecolor": "white",
+    "axes.facecolor": "white",
+})
+
+years = df["year"].astype(int)
+
+
+def make_line_chart(series, color, title, ylabel, file_name, value_format):
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 6.1))
+    ax.plot(years, series, color=color, linewidth=3, marker="o", markersize=5.5)
+    ax.fill_between(years, series, 0, color=color, alpha=0.08)
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", color=colors["ink"], pad=16)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, labelpad=10)
+    ax.set_xlabel("")
+    ax.set_xticks(years)
+    ax.set_xticklabels(years, rotation=45, ha="right")
+    ax.grid(axis="y", color=colors["grid"], linewidth=0.9)
+    ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
+    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
+    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
+    ax.spines["left"].set_visible(False)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0, pad=8)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0, pad=8)
+    ax.set_xlim(2012.7, 2025.5)
+    ax.annotate(value_format.format(series.iloc[0]), (years.iloc[0], series.iloc[0]),
+                xytext=(8, 9), textcoords="offset points", color=colors["ink"], fontweight="bold")
+    ax.annotate(value_format.format(series.iloc[-1]), (years.iloc[-1], series.iloc[-1]),
+                xytext=(-8, 10), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", color=colors["ink"], fontweight="bold")
+    fig.text(0.10, 0.035,
+             "Brooklyn · complete calendar years 2013–2025 · police-reported crashes\n"
+             "Counts are not adjusted for walking exposure. Source: NYC motor vehicle crash records.",
+             color=colors["muted"], fontsize=9)
+    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.10, right=0.97, top=0.86, bottom=0.25)
+    fig.savefig(OUT / file_name, dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+df[["year", "pedestrians_injured"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+make_line_chart(
+    df["pedestrians_injured"], colors["blue"],
+    "Brooklyn pedestrian injuries fell—then climbed back",
+    "Pedestrians injured (people per year)", "option_1.png", "{:,.0f}"
+)
+
+df[["year", "pedestrians_killed"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+make_line_chart(
+    df["pedestrians_killed"], colors["red"],
+    "Pedestrian deaths in Brooklyn remain volatile",
+    "Pedestrians killed (people per year)", "option_2.png", "{:.0f}"
+)
+
+rate_data = df[["year", "total_crash_reports", "crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty", "pedestrian_casualties_per_1000_crash_reports"]].copy()
+rate_data.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False, float_format="%.3f")
+make_line_chart(
+    df["pedestrian_casualties_per_1000_crash_reports"], colors["gold"],
+    "A larger share of Brooklyn crash reports involve pedestrian casualties",
+    "Crash reports with pedestrian injury or death per 1,000 reports",
+    "option_3.png", "{:.1f}"
+)
+
+first, last = df.iloc[0], df.iloc[-1]
+injury_change = (last["pedestrians_injured"] / first["pedestrians_injured"] - 1) * 100
+death_change = (last["pedestrians_killed"] / first["pedestrians_killed"] - 1) * 100
+rate_change = (last["pedestrian_casualties_per_1000_crash_reports"] / first["pedestrian_casualties_per_1000_crash_reports"] - 1) * 100
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians injured",
+            "denominator": "None; absolute count of injured pedestrians in police-reported Brooklyn crashes",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Annual injury counts give a direct, easily understood measure of the number of pedestrians hurt.",
+            "probability": 0.4,
+            "answer": f"This dataset cannot show risk per walking trip, but reported Brooklyn pedestrian injuries fell from {first['pedestrians_injured']:,.0f} in 2013 to {last['pedestrians_injured']:,.0f} in 2025 ({injury_change:.1f}%), after a low of {df['pedestrians_injured'].min():,.0f} in 2020.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether the annual number of pedestrians injured has declined: it fell substantially from 2013 to 2020, then rose each year through 2025. Absolute injury counts are a straightforward measure of harm, but without pedestrian exposure data they cannot show whether an individual's risk of injury per trip changed."
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed",
+            "denominator": "None; absolute count of pedestrians killed in police-reported Brooklyn crashes",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "A separate fatality series highlights the most severe pedestrian outcome, which can move differently from injuries.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
+            "answer": f"This dataset cannot show risk per walking trip, and pedestrian deaths were {first['pedestrians_killed']:.0f} in 2013 versus {last['pedestrians_killed']:.0f} in 2025 ({death_change:+.1f}%), with sizable year-to-year swings.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether the annual fatality count has fallen: it has not fallen between 2013 and 2025, though the year-by-year series is volatile. Fatality counts isolate the gravest outcome, but they do not measure individual pedestrian risk or explain why counts changed."
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Brooklyn crash reports with at least one pedestrian injured or killed per 1,000 crash reports",
+            "denominator": "All police-reported Brooklyn motor vehicle crashes in the same calendar year",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Normalizing by all reported crashes distinguishes pedestrian-casualty crashes from the overall volume of reported crashes.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": f"This dataset cannot show risk per walking trip, but pedestrian-casualty crashes rose from {first['crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty'] / first['total_crash_reports'] * 1000:.1f} to {last['crashes_with_pedestrian_casualty'] / last['total_crash_reports'] * 1000:.1f} per 1,000 reported Brooklyn crashes from 2013 to 2025 ({rate_change:+.1f}%).",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers how often reported crashes involved pedestrian injury or death relative to the total volume of Brooklyn crash reports: that share was higher in 2025 than in 2013. It accounts for changes in crash-report volume, but its denominator is crashes rather than people walking or walking trips, so it cannot establish pedestrian exposure-adjusted safety."
+        }
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
*** End Patch
